name: Thien Mu Pagoda
kicker: Seven-tiered tower on the north bank
summary: The seven-tiered Phước Duyên tower on Hà Khê hill above the Perfume River, at a pagoda founded by Nguyễn Hoàng in the early 17th century. Ride upstream along the north bank through Kim Long, then walk up from the river to the tower and the hall behind it. Go in the late afternoon for the tower and the river together, or stop on the way to a tomb.
getThere: Along the north bank through Kim Long, by bicycle or taxi.
heroCaption: The tower and the pagoda hall at Thien Mu

notice.title: Not on the monument ticket
notice.body: Thien Mu is not on the fee table that prices the Imperial City and the tombs, and the centre’s visiting-hours notice does not list it. Ask at the gate about any fee and the hours.

body: The tower is the reason to stop. Vietnam Tourism calls out the seven tiers. The culture department, writing a river trip, describes the Phước Duyên tower rising over Hà Khê hill and the pines, and dates the pagoda to Nguyễn Hoàng in the early 17th century. The ranked-monument list puts it in Kim Long and names the conservation centre and the city’s Buddhist association as the managers.

UNESCO lists Thien Mu among the monuments outside the Capital City. Treat it as a stop on the way upstream, not as a second palace. Late afternoon is the hour if the tower and the river are the picture. Morning is enough if you are already riding toward a tomb.
Kim Long, the road you ride in on, is also the road for bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng. Eat on the way back.

figures.caption: The Phước Duyên tower from below, with the spire in the frame
figures.alt: The octagonal brick tower of Thien Mu Pagoda rising against a blue sky, seen from below

gettingThere: Thien Mu is in Kim Long, on the north bank upstream of the citadel. Ride along that bank by bicycle, or take a taxi.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: Cross to the north bank and follow the river upstream through Kim Long.

closed: Not covered by the centre’s visiting-hours notice. Confirm at the gate.
admissionNote: Check on arrival. Resolution 55/2025/NQ-HĐND, in force 4 January 2026, does not list Thien Mu; that is not proof of free entry.
